description: A many-stemmed shrub 2-4 m tall with glossy, pointed leaves in pairs or threes, and in summer round white flower balls the size of a golf ball, bristling with long styles like pins in a pincushion. It stands with its feet in the water at the edges of ponds, sloughs and slow reaches of the creeks, and its seed balls turn brown and hang on into winter.

season_notes.winter: Bare, crooked grey-brown stems standing in the water, hung with brown, knobbly seed balls.
season_notes.spring: Leafs out late, in April and May, bright glossy green.
season_notes.summer: White pincushion flower balls from June to August, sweet-scented, crowded with bees and butterflies.
season_notes.fall: The flower balls ripen to hard reddish-brown spheres; the leaves yellow and drop.

riparian.water: Stands in shallow, slow or still water or in mud that stays saturated all summer: pond edges, sloughs, backwaters and slow pools, not the fast riffles.

notes: Buttonbush (button willow) is a deciduous shrub 1-5 m of pond and lake edges, sloughs, backwaters and slow, permanent reaches, in California mostly in the Central Valley and the low foothills (below about 500 m here, at the bottom of the game's range); it is one of the few woody plants that grows standing in water for months. Form: plain 'shrub'. Four to eight crooked, often leaning stems with swollen, buttressed bases in the water (stems [4, 8], flare 1.35, sinuous), branching in pairs or threes (rotation -90: opposite to whorled), into a rounded, irregular, open crown a little wider than tall. Bark grey-brown, becoming furrowed on old trunks (bark_pattern furrowed). Leaves opposite or in whorls of three, ovate to lanceolate, 7-15 cm, pointed, glossy bright green: leaf_shape elliptic_glossy, leaf_size_m 0.11. It leafs out late (April-May) and is bare December-March (leaf_on_by_month). Flowers in dense spherical heads 2-4 cm, white to cream, with long protruding styles (the pincushion), June-August: flowers form bud (a round knob is the closest form), size_m 0.035, white. Fruit the same ball ripening to a hard reddish-brown cluster of nutlets that hangs on the bare stems into winter: berries form bud, brown, months [9, 1]. The foliage is reported toxic to livestock and is little browsed (eaten_by: deer, summer, lightly); its seeds feed waterfowl, which the game has none of yet. Zones: the margin and the pond shore first (it stands in the water), the bank of slow reaches; permanence perennial; orders [2, 7] where the water is slow. Architectural model provisional.
